model.rationale: Every available signal points the same direction: a D+13 district, a six-term incumbent with a nearly 30-to-1 fundraising edge, and markets pricing this at about 97% Democratic. With no polling to the contrary, the margin sits near the low twenties and the race is rated Safe D.
model.watch: A major national wave against Democrats or an unforeseen scandal involving Himes would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Connecticut's 4th District is anchored in wealthy Fairfield County suburbs and leans Democratic by roughly 13 points. Jim Himes, first elected in 2008, has consistently won reelection by wide margins and enters this cycle as a heavy favorite. His Republican challenger, Michael Goldstein, has raised only about $58,000 and had roughly $25,000 on hand, leaving him badly outmatched in resources.

Himes has raised nearly $1.7 million and holds about $2.4 million in cash, with no outside groups spending against him. No public general-election polling is available, and no major expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets price Himes at about 97 percent to win. Fundamentals, money, and market pricing all align on a comfortable Democratic hold, with only an extraordinary external shock plausibly putting the outcome in doubt.
